Rashi on Niddah 8a:10:1.hebrew: וכן אמר ר' אלעזר - אדשמואל קאי. ואמורא הוא, והוא ר' אלעזר בן פדת. ורבי אלעזר דמיאון תנא הוא, והוא ר' אלעזר בן שמוע:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:10:1.english: And so said Rabbi Elazar - It refers to [the statement of] Shmuel. And he is an Amora, and he is Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat; whereas the Rabbi Elazar of refusal [mi'un] is a Tanna, and he is Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:11:1.english: The rose and the henna - They are types of spices.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:11:2.hebrew: קטף - מין אילן, ואין עושה פרי אלא שרף (יוצא ונוטף מהן), וזהו פריו:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:11:2.english: Balsam - A species of tree, and it does not produce fruit, but rather sap (which emerges and drips from them), and this is its fruit.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:11:3.hebrew: יש להן שביעית - שצריך להפקירם, ואסור לעשות בהן סחורה, ולא אמרי' עצים בעלמא נינהו ושביעית אינה נוהגת בעצים, כדאמרי' בלולב הגזול (סוכה דף מ.):
Rashi on Niddah 8a:11:3.english: They are subject to the Sabbatical Year - That one must declare them ownerless, and it is forbidden to engage in commerce with them, and we do not say they are mere wood and the Sabbatical Year does not apply to wood, as we say in [chapter] Lulav HaGazul (Sukkah 40a).

Rashi on Niddah 8a:11:4.hebrew: ביעור - כשכלה לחיה מן השדה. ואע"ג דיש להן שביעית, איצטריך למימר יש להן ביעור, דיש שיש לו שביעית ליאסר בסחורה ומלוגמא ואין לו ביעור, כגון דבר המתקיים בארץ כל ימי החורף, שאינה כלה לחיה מן השדה. אבל כל דבר שיש לו ביעור, יש לו שביעית:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:11:4.english: Removal - [This takes effect] when [produce of that species] is finished for the wild animal from the field. And even though they are subject to [the sanctity of the] Sabbatical Year, it was necessary to state [that] they are subject to removal, for there is [produce] that is subject to [the sanctity of the] Sabbatical Year—to be forbidden for commerce and [for use as] a poultice—and is not subject to removal, such as an item that endures in the ground all through the days of winter, so that it is not finished for the wild animal from the field. However, anything that is subject to removal is subject to [the sanctity of the] Sabbatical Year.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:11:5.english: And Rabbi Pedat said - [He was] the son of Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:11:6.hebrew: מאן תנא - להא דקתני יש להן שביעית, דקסבר קטפא פירא? ר' אליעזר, כדאמר לקמן: ר"א אומר: המעמיד בשרף הערלה אסור:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:11:6.english: Who is the tanna - [Who taught] that which was taught: "They have [the sanctity of] the Sabbatical Year," holding that balsam sap is fruit? [It is] Rabbi Eliezer, as [the Gemara] states later: "Rabbi Eliezer says: One who curdles [cheese] with the sap of orlah, it is forbidden."

Rashi on Niddah 8a:12:1.english: You have permitted balsam - With regard to the Sabbatical Year.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:12:2.english: In accordance with Rabbi Eliezer in four [cases] - And no more. It follows that regarding balsam [being considered] fruit, he does not act in accordance with his opinion [even] to be stringent.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:16:1.hebrew: אומרה ברכה רביעית - להבדלה במוצאי שבתות, ואינו כוללה בחונן הדעת:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:16:1.english: One recites it as a fourth blessing - [This refers to] Havdalah on Saturday nights, and one does not include it in [the blessing of] Chonen HaDa'at.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:16:2.english: And Rabbi Elazar said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer - [This is stated] in the Jerusalem Talmud, [tractate] Berakhot.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:1:1.hebrew: מלמדין את הקטנה - בפרק בית שמאי ביבמות: ב' אחין נשואין ב' אחיות יתומות, אחת גדולה ואחת קטנה. מת בעלה של גדולה, ונמצאת זקוקה ליבם בעל הקטנה, ודוחה זיקתה נישואי אחותה הקטנה ואוסרתה עליו, שאין נישואי קטנה כלום. ואם יגרשנה לקטנה בגט, שוב אינו יכול ליבם את הגדולה, שאחות גרושתו היא; אלא מלמדין את הקטנה שתמאן בו, ומיאון עוקר נישואין הראשונים, ומותר ליבם הגדולה:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:1:1.english: We instruct the minor - In the chapter "Beit Shammai" in Yevamot: Two brothers are married to two orphaned sisters, one an adult and one a minor. The husband of the adult died, and she is bound to the levir, the husband of the minor, and her levirate bond overrides the marriage of her minor sister and forbids her [the minor] to him, for the marriage of a minor is nothing [under Torah law]. And if he divorces the minor with a bill of divorce [get], he can no longer perform levirate marriage with the adult, as she is the sister of his divorcee. Rather, we instruct the minor to refuse him, and refusal [mi'un] uproots the initial marriage, and he is permitted to perform levirate marriage with the adult.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:2:1.hebrew: הרודה ונותן לסל - כגון שהיה לש את עיסתו פחות פחות מחמשת רבעים, לפוטרו מן החלה:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:2:1.english: One who removes [loaves from the oven] and places [them] into a basket - For example, where he was kneading his dough in [batches of] less than five quarters [of a kav], to exempt it from challah.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:2:2.english: The basket combines them - When he removes them from the oven.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:3:1.hebrew: מאי אולמיה דהאי - דחלה מההיא דמיאון, דפשטת לה מינה דאמרת ה"נ מסתברא? הא שמעינן מההיא דמיאון דבשאר סדרי איכא הלכה כר"א:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:3:1.english: What is the strength of this - [The case] of challah over that [case] of refusal, that you resolved it from it, when you said, "This too stands to reason"? After all, we learned from that [case] of refusal that in the other orders there is [a case where] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:3:2.hebrew: ומשני: מההיא דמיאון ליכא למשמע מינה דבשאר סדרים איכא, דהתם משום דקאי ר' אלעזר כר"א, ואיכא למימר: משום דמסייע ר' אלעזר לר"א, מש"ה הלכה כמותו בהא, אבל משום דידיה לחודיה לא:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:3:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: From that [case] of refusal [mi'un], it cannot be inferred that in the other orders there are [cases where the halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer], as there, [it is] because Rabbi Elazar holds in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, and it can be said: Because Rabbi Elazar supports Rabbi Eliezer, that is why the halakha is in accordance with him in this [case], but on his own account alone, no.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:4:1.english: One instructs the minor - This is regarding a different matter in chapter Beit Shammai [in Yevamot].

Rashi on Niddah 8a:5:1.hebrew: ומי קאי והא אצרוכי מצרכינן ליה - התם, דאמר שמואל בקמייתא: הלכה כר"א, ובאידך נמי: הלכה כר' אלעזר, ואמרי': צריכא, דאי אשמועינן כו'. אלמא ר' אלעזר ור"א לאו חד טעמא קאמרי, מדאיצטריך לשמואל למימר בתרווייהו הלכה:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:5:1.english: And does he stand [with him]? But don't we require it - There [in tractate Yevamot], where Shmuel said on the first [mishna]: "The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer," and on the other [mishna] as well: "The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar," and we said [there]: "[Both] are necessary, for had he taught us..." etc. Evidently, Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Eliezer do not state [their rulings based on] a single rationale, since it was necessary for Shmuel to state "the halakha [is in accordance with him]" in both of them.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:6:1.hebrew: שממאנין את הקטנות - מבקשין מהן שימאנו, כגון הנך דרבי אלעזר ור"א, כדי לקיים מצות יבום:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:6:1.english: That one causes minor girls to refuse - We request of them that they refuse, such as those [cases] of Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Eliezer, in order to fulfill the mitzvah of levirate marriage.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:7:1.hebrew: ושמשיאין אשה - שהלך בעלה למדינת הים, ושמעה מפי עד אחד שמת, משיאין אותה לאחר:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:7:1.english: And that they marry off a woman - Where her husband went overseas, and she heard from a single witness that he died, they marry her off to another.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:7:2.hebrew: ושנסקל תרנגול - כדכתיב (שמות כ״א:כ״ט) והמית איש או אשה השור יסקל, והוא הדין לכל חיה ועוף, כדאוקימנא בשור שנגח את הפרה (ב"ק דף נד:) דיליף שור שור משבת, אלא שדבר הכתוב בהווה:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:7:2.english: And that a rooster was stoned - As it is written (Exodus 21:29): "And it killed a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned," and the same law applies to all beasts and birds, as we established in [the chapter] "An ox that gored a cow" (Bava Kamma 54b), where [the Gemara] derives [the law via a gezeirah shavah of] "ox" [and] "ox" from Shabbat; rather, Scripture spoke of the prevalent [case].

Rashi on Niddah 8a:7:3.hebrew: בן מ' יום - ומקמי הכי פסול, דה"ל יין מגתו:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:7:3.english: Forty days old - And prior to this it is disqualified, for it is wine from its vat.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:8:1.hebrew: קטנות דעלמא - ולעולם עדות בן בבא אדר' אלעזר קאי ולא אדר"א, וה"ק: כל קטנות שיבאו למאן לפנינו כי ההיא דר"א, מלמדין אותן למאן:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:8:1.english: Minor girls in general - And actually, the testimony of [Rabbi Yehuda] ben Bava refers to [the case of] Rabbi Elazar, and not to [that of] Rabbi Eliezer; and this is what it is saying: All minor girls who come to refuse before us like that [case] of Rabbi Elazar, we instruct them to refuse.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:9:1.english: Let it teach: Women - [I.e.,] that they marry off women based on the testimony of one witness.

Rashi on Niddah 8a:9:2.english: And let us say: What is [meant by] "women"? Women in general - Just as [the Gemara] said: "What is [meant by] 'minor girls'? Minor girls in general."

Rashi on Niddah 8a:9:3.hebrew: דוקא קתני - קטנות שתים: אחת דר' אלעזר ואחת דר' אליעזר, ואשה דליכא למימר הכי, נסבה בלשון יחיד:
Rashi on Niddah 8a:9:3.english: He taught specifically - [The plural] "minor girls" [means] two: one of Rabbi Elazar and one of Rabbi Eliezer; and [as for] a woman, where one cannot say this, he phrased it in the singular.

Tosafot on Niddah 8a:11:1.hebrew: יש להן ביעור ולדמיהם ביעור - אע"ג דשביעית תופסת דמיה, יש חילוק בביעור בין דמיה לעצמה, כדתנן בפ"ב דשביעית: ר' מאיר אומר, דמיה מתבערים עד ר"ה, אבל הן מתבערין עד הפסח:
Tosafot on Niddah 8a:11:1.english: They have [the law of] removal, and their proceeds have [the law of] removal - Even though [produce of the] Sabbatical Year captures its proceeds [transferring its sanctity to them], there is a distinction regarding removal between its proceeds and [the produce] itself, as we learned in the second chapter of Shevi'it: Rabbi Meir says, its proceeds are removed until Rosh HaShanah, but they [themselves] are removed until Pesach.

Tosafot on Niddah 8a:11:2.hebrew: קטף - פירש רש"י: שם העץ. וכן בברייתא פ"ק דכריתות (דף ו.): רשב"ג אומר, הצרי אינו אלא שרף מעצי הקטף. ושרף עצמו נקרא קטף על שם העץ, כדאמר הכא דיש בו שביעית, ובסמוך נמי אמר דקטפו זהו פריו, וצרי ולוט (בראשית ל״ז:כ״ה) מתרגמינן קטף ולוטא. ומה שפירש"י דאינו עושה פירות, אלא שרף נוטף ממנו וזהו פריו, אינו למאי דמוקי ליה ר' זירא בסמוך בקטפא דפירא: [ונראה דרש"י פירש כן לשינויא בתרא. גי':]
Tosafot on Niddah 8a:11:2.english: Balsam (kataf) - Rashi explained: [It is] the name of the tree. And so [it is taught] in a baraita in the first chapter of Keritot (6a): "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: The balm (tzeri) is nothing other than sap from balsam trees (atzei ha-kataf)." And the sap itself is called kataf after the name of the tree, as it says here that it has [the sanctity of the] Sabbatical Year, and shortly it also says: "for its katef is its fruit"; and [in the verse] "balm and ladanum" (Genesis 37:25), we translate [in the Targum]: "kataf ve-lota". And that which Rashi explained, that "it does not produce fruit, but rather sap drips from it and that is its fruit" — this does not accord with that which Rabbi Zeira establishes shortly [as referring to] the sap of the fruit (katfa de-feira). [And it appears that Rashi explained thus according to the latter resolution. — Gloss.]

Tosafot on Niddah 8a:11:3.hebrew: ואמר רבי פדת מאן תנא כו' - ואם תאמר, דבפרק קמא דברכות (דף ה:) אמר ליה ר' יוחנן לרבי אלעזר: אי משום בני, דין גרמא דעשיראה ביר, משמע דלרבי אלעזר לא היו לו בנים? ויש לומר, שאחרי כן נולד לו; או היו לו בנים הרבה ומתו מקצתם, ואמר ליה רבי יוחנן כך כדי לנחמו:
Tosafot on Niddah 8a:11:3.english: And Rabbi Pedat said: Who is the Tanna, etc. - And if you say that in the first chapter of Berakhot (5b), Rabbi Yochanan said to Rabbi Elazar: "If [it is] on account of children, this is the bone of [my] tenth son," which implies that Rabbi Elazar had no children? One can say that afterwards [a son] was born to him; or, he had many children and some of them died, and Rabbi Yochanan said this to him in order to comfort him.

Tosafot on Niddah 8a:11:4.hebrew: מאן תנא דאמר קטפא פירא ר' אליעזר - ואם תאמר: במאי פליגי? אי ביעורו והנאתו שוה, מאי טעמא דרבנן? דאפי' עצים הוו אסירי בשביעית, אי לאו דאין הנאתו וביעורו שוה. ואי אין הנאתו וביעורו שוה, לא אסור בשביעית. ואין סברא לומר דפליגי אי הנאתו וביעורו שוה אי לאו. ויש לומר: דודאי הנאתו וביעורו שוה, ולפי שאינו כי אם לחלוחי העץ, שרו רבנן, דבטל אגב העץ; ורבי אליעזר סבר, דהנאתו חשיבא והוי פירי:
Tosafot on Niddah 8a:11:4.english: Who is the Tanna who said that balsam sap (kataf) is fruit? Rabbi Eliezer - And if you say: In what do they disagree? If its destruction and its benefit are simultaneous, what is the Rabbis' reason [for exempting it]? For even wood would have been forbidden in the Sabbatical Year, were it not that its benefit and destruction are not simultaneous. And if its benefit and destruction are not simultaneous, it would not be forbidden in the Sabbatical Year [even according to Rabbi Eliezer]! And it is not reasonable to say that they disagree [as to] whether its benefit and destruction are simultaneous or not. And one can say: Certainly its benefit and destruction are simultaneous. But because it is nothing other than the moisture of the wood, the Rabbis permit it, for it is subordinate to the wood; whereas Rabbi Eliezer holds that its benefit is significant, and [therefore] it constitutes fruit.

Tosafot on Niddah 8a:12:1.hebrew: ואבוך אמר הלכה כר"א בד' - אע"ג דר' יוסי קאי כוותיה, דבהגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף קב.) אית להו דשביעית נוהגת בעצים, וא"כ כ"ש קטפא; ומשום דרבי יוסי קאי כותיה לא חשיב ליה עם הנך? דטעמא דר' יוסי משום דלא בעי הנאתו וביעורו שוה, ולא קיימא לן כוותיה, אלא אין שביעית נוהגת בעצים; דר' יוסי נמי מודה דקטפא לאו פירא הוא לענין ערלה:
Tosafot on Niddah 8a:12:1.english: And your father said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer in four [cases] - Even though Rabbi Yose stands with him [Rabbi Eliezer] — as in HaGozel Kama (Bava Kamma 102a) they hold that the Sabbatical Year applies to wood, and if so, all the more so to balsam — [could it be that] because Rabbi Yose stands with him, he did not reckon it among those [four]? [No, for] Rabbi Yose's reason is that he does not require its benefit and its destruction to be concurrent, and we do not hold in accordance with him, but rather [we hold that] the Sabbatical Year does not apply to wood; for Rabbi Yose also agrees that balsam is not fruit regarding [the laws of] orlah.

Tosafot on Niddah 8a:15:1.hebrew: [משום דקאי רבי יהודה בן בבא כותיה - אע"ג דבמתני' נמי חזר בו ר' יהושע וקאי כוותיה, ואפ"ה מני לה בד'. וי"ל, דשמא ר' יהושע סבר כר' יוסי, דמצריך ג' עונות במעוברת ומניקה, דפליג ארבי אליעזר, ולא הדר ביה אלא ממה שאמר: אני לא שמעתי אלא בתולה. גי':]
Tosafot on Niddah 8a:15:1.english: [Because Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava holds in accordance with him - Even though in our mishna as well, Rabbi Yehoshua retracted and held in accordance with him, and nevertheless he [the Amora] counted it among the four [cases]? And it can be said that perhaps Rabbi Yehoshua held in accordance with Rabbi Yose, who requires three periods (onot) for a pregnant woman and a nursing woman, who disagrees with Rabbi Eliezer; and he retracted only from what he had said: "I only heard [this rule regarding] a virgin." — Marginal gloss]

Tosafot on Niddah 8a:7:1.hebrew: ועל היין בן מ' יום - פרש"י דקודם לכן הוי יין מגתו. אע"ג דאמרי' בהמוכר פירות (ב"ב דף צז.) יין מגתו אם הביא כשר, בן מ' יום לכתחילה נמי יביא, אפילו יש הרבה מיין אחר:
Tosafot on Niddah 8a:7:1.english: And regarding forty-day-old wine - Rashi explained that prior to this it is [considered] wine from its press. Even though we say in [the chapter] HaMokher Peirot (Bava Batra 97a) that wine from its press, if one brought [it], is valid, [wine that is] forty days old one may even bring [it] ab initio, even if there is plenty of other wine.
